Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its normed additive commutative group structure, a measurable-space structure, and the assertion that this structure is its Borel measurable structure. Write
\[
d=\dim_{\mathbb R}E,
\]
viewed as a real number, and assume \(d>0\).

Let \(V:E\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\alpha,\beta\) be nonnegative real numbers. Assume:

1. \(0<\alpha\le\beta\).
2. \(V\) is \(C^2\) over \(\mathbb R\).
3. For every \(x,w\in E\),
   \[
   \alpha\|w\|^2
   \le D(DV)(x)[w][w]
   \le\beta\|w\|^2.
   \]

Define the state space
\[
S=\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times E\times E\times\mathbb N\times E^{\mathbb N}.
\]
For clarity, write a state as \(s=(a,c,u,k,h)\), where \(h:\mathbb N\to E\) is a full infinite sequence. Use the corresponding product measurable structure.

Let \(\eta,\tau:S\to\mathbb R\) be any measurable functions satisfying
\[
\eta(s)>0,\qquad \tau(s)>0
\quad\text{for every }s\in S.
\]
Let \(M:S\rightsquigarrow E\) be any Markov kernel, and let \(\theta\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) be any threshold.

In the following formulas, nonnegative real numbers are coerced to real numbers when used in real arithmetic. Define
\[
v(s)=\frac{\eta(s)+\tau(s)}{\beta+a},
\qquad
b(s)=a+\operatorname{toNNReal}\bigl(v(s)^{-1}\bigr).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{toNNReal}(r)=\max(r,0)\), interpreted as a nonnegative real. The stated assumptions imply \(\beta+a>0\) and \(v(s)>0\), so the truncation does not change the inverse.

For \(p=(s,(y,z))\in S\times(E\times E)\), define
\[
o(p)=y+\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{\beta+a}}\,z,
\]
\[
m(p)=b(s)^{-1}\bigl(ac+v(s)^{-1}o(p)\bigr),
\]
\[
F_p(x)=V(x)+\frac{b(s)}2\|x-m(p)\|^2,
\]
and the map
\[
G_p(x)=x-\frac1{\beta+b(s)}\nabla F_p(x).
\]
Scalar multiplication is the real scalar action on \(E\). All square roots are real square roots.

For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), set
\[
q_n(p)=\left\|\nabla F_p\bigl(G_p^{[n]}(y)\bigr)\right\|^2,
\]
where \(G_p^{[n]}\) is the \(n\)-fold iterate and the zeroth iterate is the identity. Define a total natural-valued function by
\[
N(p)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{n\in\mathbb N:q_n(p)\le(\alpha+b(s))d\},
&\text{if this set is nonempty},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\[
r(p)=G_p^{[N(p)]}(y).
\]
The update map \(U:S\times(E\times E)\to S\) is
\[
U(p)=\bigl(b(s),m(p),r(p),k+1,h_p'\bigr),
\]
where
\[
h_p'(0)=o(p),\qquad h_p'(n+1)=h(n)\quad(n\in\mathbb N).
\]
In particular, the iteration starts at the newly supplied coordinate \(y\); the existing state coordinate \(u\) does not explicitly appear in these update formulas. The functions \(\eta,\tau\) and the kernel \(M\) may nevertheless depend on every coordinate of \(s\).

Let \(\lambda_E\) denote canonical Lebesgue volume on \(E\), and define
\[
\mu=\operatorname{Tilt}(\lambda_E,-V).
\]
The notation \(\operatorname{Tilt}(\nu,f)\) means the total, normalized exponential reweighting operation in the provided Lean API. Its notation alone is not an assumption of finite normalization or probability.

Then \(\mu\) is a probability measure. Moreover, there exist Markov kernels
\[
A:S\rightsquigarrow E,\qquad
H:S\rightsquigarrow E,\qquad
P:S\rightsquigarrow S
\]
with all of the following properties.

For every \(s=(a,c,u,k,h)\in S\),
\[
A(s)=\operatorname{Tilt}
\left(\mu,\;x\mapsto-\frac a2\|x-c\|^2\right).
\]

Writing \(\gamma_E\) for the standard Gaussian probability measure on \(E\), for every \(s\in S\),
\[
H(s)=
\operatorname{Law}(X+\sqrt{v(s)}Z),
\]
where \(X\sim A(s)\) and \(Z\sim\gamma_E\) are independent. Precisely, this is the pushforward under addition of the product of \(A(s)\) with the pushforward of \(\gamma_E\) under \(z\mapsto\sqrt{v(s)}z\).

For every \(s=(a,c,u,k,h)\in S\),
\[
P(s)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_s,&\theta\le a,\\
\operatorname{Law}\bigl(U(s,(Y,Z))\bigr),&a<\theta,
\end{cases}
\]
where in the second branch \(Y\sim M(s)\) and \(Z\sim\gamma_E\) independently.

Define, for all states, the probability measure
\[
Q(s)=
\operatorname{Law}
\left(Y+\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{\beta+a}}Z\right),
\]
with \(Y\sim M(s)\) and \(Z\sim\gamma_E\) independently. Define
\[
e(s)=
\begin{cases}
0,&\theta\le a,\\
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(Q(s)\|H(s)),&a<\theta.
\end{cases}
\]
Then \(e:S\to[0,\infty]\) is measurable.

For every Markov kernel \(R:S\rightsquigarrow E\), the function
\[
s\longmapsto D_{\mathrm{KL}}(R(s)\|A(s))
\]
is measurable, and for every \(s\in S\),
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl((R\circ P)(s)\|A(s)\bigr)
\le
e(s)+
\int_S D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(R(t)\|A(t)\bigr)\,P(s,dt).
\]
Here \((R\circ P)(s)\) first draws \(t\sim P(s)\) and then draws an \(E\)-valued output from \(R(t)\). The reference measure on the left is \(A(s)\) at the original state; the reference measure inside the integral is \(A(t)\) at the intermediate state.

The existential choice of \(A,H,P\) precedes the universal quantification over \(R\): the same three kernels work for every Markov kernel \(R\). All conclusions hold pointwise for every state, not merely almost everywhere.

Relative entropy and the integral take values in the extended nonnegative reals. There is no assumed finiteness, absolute continuity, or integrability of the displayed relative entropies. If the right-hand side is infinite, the asserted inequality has its usual extended-order meaning. The hypotheses require no additional approximation, density, regularity, or accuracy condition on \(M\) or \(R\) beyond their being Markov kernels.

The displayed theorem does not separately assert that the set defining \(N(p)\) is nonempty, a bound on \(N(p)\), or a finite evaluation cost. Its definition expressly includes the empty-set fallback \(N(p)=0\). No quantitative iteration bound or additional assertion about the fallback is part of the reconstructed conclusion.

The formulas contain no unspecified constants. Their numerical dependencies are exactly the displayed dimension \(d\), curvature parameters \(\alpha,\beta\), functions \(\eta,\tau\), current state coordinates, and supplied potential \(V\). The threshold affects the branch defining \(P\) and \(e\); \(M\) supplies the random first input to the active update and to \(Q\).
